name: Saint Louis Grignion de Montfort
history: A Breton priest who walked the roads of western France preaching missions to the poor, singing hymns he wrote himself and setting up great calvaries. Often opposed and expelled, he founded the Company of Mary and, with Blessed Marie-Louise Trichet, the Daughters of Wisdom. His True Devotion to Mary taught total consecration to Jesus through Mary.
life: Louis-Marie Grignion was born at Montfort-sur-Meu in Brittany, studied at Saint-Sulpice in Paris and was ordained in 1700. As chaplain of the hospital at Poitiers he met Marie-Louise Trichet, with whom he founded the Daughters of Wisdom to care for the sick and poor. His blunt preaching and his austerity made enemies, and he was more than once forbidden to preach in a diocese. In 1706 he walked to Rome, and Pope Clement XI named him missionary apostolic. Back in France he preached some two hundred missions, mostly in country parishes, restored churches, wrote a great many hymns and built a huge calvary at Pontchâteau, which the authorities ordered pulled down. His treatise on True Devotion lay hidden until 1842 and has since shaped millions, among them John Paul II, whose motto Totus Tuus came from it. He died at Saint-Laurent-sur-Sèvre in 1716, aged forty-three.
prayerTo: Saint Louis de Montfort, you gave yourself wholly to Jesus through Mary and spent your life for the poor. Pray for missionaries and for all who preach the Gospel to the forgotten. Teach me to belong entirely to Christ through His Mother, and to bear opposition with patience and joy. Amen.
penance: Pray the Rosary today, or one decade if time is short, and give it to Our Lady for her to use as she wills. Do a kindness for someone who is poor or sick.
meditation: Totus tuus: I am all yours. Is there any part of your life you have kept back from Christ?
